settings.tagline: The GraphQL-first headless CMS in a single Rust binary
settings.description: Tess is a self-hostable, GraphQL-first headless CMS written in Rust. Define content models at runtime, publish with review workflows, and run it on Docker, a VM or AWS Lambda.
settings.footerText: © 2026 Tess Dev Team. Community edition for personal use, Enterprise edition for commercial use.

data.title: Compare Tess with other CMSs
data.description: How Tess compares with Strapi, Hygraph, WordPress, Contentful, Directus, Payload, and Sanity: architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, hosting and license.

competitors.name: Strapi
competitors.summary: The most popular open-source headless CMS, built on Node.js, with a REST API and a GraphQL plugin.

rows.other: Node.js (TypeScript) application

rows.tess: Created at runtime in production (admin or API); the GraphQL schema is regenerated live
rows.other: Content-Type Builder in development mode; models are saved as code files and deployed with the app
REST by default, GraphQL through an official plugin

rows.tess: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB, RocksDB
rows.other: PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite

rows.tess: Per content type, in every edition
rows.other: Draft & publish included; review workflows in paid plans

rows.tess: Sandboxed WebAssembly modules installed at runtime
rows.other: Node.js packages running in the app process, large marketplace
Built-in internationalization of content

rows.tess: Self-hosted: Docker, VM, Kubernetes or AWS Lambda
rows.other: Self-hosted or Strapi Cloud
MIT for the Community Edition; paid plans for enterprise features

competitors.chooseThem:
- You want a large plugin marketplace and community.
- You need localized content today.
- Your team prefers to customize the CMS itself in JavaScript/TypeScript.
competitors.chooseTess:
- Editors or admins must change models **in production**, without a redeploy.
- You want a GraphQL-first API on MongoDB, DynamoDB or an embedded database.
- You want a review workflow without a paid plan, or to run on AWS Lambda.
competitors.migration: Strapi types map closely to Tess: `string`/`text` → `TEXT`, `richtext` → `MARKDOWN`, `blocks` → `JSON`, `enumeration` → `ENUM`, `relation` → `RELATION`, `media` → `RELATION` to `Asset`, `component` → `COMPONENT`, `dynamiczone` → `DYNAMIC_ZONE`. Write your models in the `tess-transfer` YAML format and import them in one command, then copy the entries through the GraphQL API.

competitors.name: Hygraph
competitors.summary: A hosted, GraphQL-native CMS (formerly GraphCMS), known for content federation across remote APIs.

rows.other: Managed SaaS only
GraphQL generated from the models, with content federation of remote sources

rows.tess: Admin UI or API, applied immediately
rows.other: Schema editor in the web app, with environments
Hygraph's cloud, in the regions it offers

rows.tess: Per content type, in every edition
rows.other: Content stages and workflows, depending on the plan
Built-in localization
UI extensions, webhooks and remote sources

rows.tess: Community free for personal use; Enterprise license for commercial use
rows.other: Free tier, then paid plans by usage and features

competitors.chooseThem:
- You don't want to operate any infrastructure.
- You need content federation or built-in localization.
competitors.chooseTess:
- Your content must stay on your own infrastructure or database.
- You want the same GraphQL-first experience without usage-based pricing.
competitors.migration: Hygraph's schema translates directly: models become content types, components become components, and union/modular fields become `DYNAMIC_ZONE` fields. Describe them in the `tess-transfer` YAML format, import them, then copy the entries with a GraphQL-to-GraphQL script.

competitors.name: WordPress
competitors.summary: The world's most used CMS, a PHP application with themes, plugins and a REST API, often used headless through WPGraphQL.

rows.tess: Headless: content only, any front end
rows.other: Monolithic site builder with themes; headless through its APIs

rows.tess: Typed models with validation, defined in the admin or API
rows.other: Posts and pages; custom post types and fields through code or plugins such as ACF
REST API built in; GraphQL through the WPGraphQL plugin
PHP with MySQL or MariaDB

rows.tess: Draft, review, publish per content type
rows.other: Draft, pending review and publish; more through plugins
Tens of thousands of PHP plugins and themes
GPLv2 or later

competitors.chooseThem:
- You want a website with themes, built by non-developers.
- You rely on a specific WordPress plugin or the huge ecosystem.
competitors.chooseTess:
- Your content feeds several front ends (sites, mobile apps, kiosks).
- You want structured, validated content and a typed API instead of posts and meta fields.
competitors.migration: Model your post types and custom fields as Tess content types (ACF field groups map well to components), import them with `tess-transfer`, then move the posts from the WordPress REST API to the Tess GraphQL API with a short script.

competitors.name: Contentful
competitors.summary: An enterprise headless CMS delivered as SaaS, with REST and GraphQL delivery APIs and a large app ecosystem.

rows.other: Managed SaaS only
REST delivery and management APIs, plus a GraphQL Content API

rows.tess: Admin UI or API, applied immediately
rows.other: Web app or management API, with environments
Contentful's cloud
Built-in locales
App Framework and marketplace

rows.tess: Community free for personal use; Enterprise license for commercial use
rows.other: Free tier, then paid plans with usage limits

competitors.chooseThem: - You need an enterprise SaaS with SLAs, many locales and a large app marketplace.
competitors.chooseTess:
- You want to own the infrastructure and the data.
- You prefer a predictable license to usage-based limits.
competitors.migration: Contentful content types and their fields map to Tess content types; references become `RELATION` fields and assets become `Asset` relations. Import the models with `tess-transfer`, then copy entries with the Contentful export and the Tess GraphQL API.

competitors.name: Directus
competitors.summary: A Node.js platform that turns an existing SQL database into REST and GraphQL APIs with an admin app.

rows.tess: Tess owns its storage and schema
rows.other: Mirrors the tables of an existing SQL database

rows.tess: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB, RocksDB
rows.other: SQL databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, MS SQL, Oracle, CockroachDB
REST and GraphQL
Built with permissions and Flows
Flows (event-driven automation) built in
Business Source License: free under a revenue threshold, commercial license above

competitors.chooseThem:
- You must expose an existing SQL database as is.
- You want built-in automation flows.
competitors.chooseTess:
- You start from content models, not from existing tables.
- You need NoSQL (MongoDB, DynamoDB) or an embedded database, or AWS Lambda.
competitors.migration: Each Directus collection becomes a Tess content type, and its relational fields become `RELATION` fields. Write them in the `tess-transfer` YAML format, import them, then copy the items through both GraphQL APIs.

competitors.name: Payload
competitors.summary: An open-source TypeScript CMS configured in code, which installs inside a Next.js application.

rows.tess: Defined at runtime in the admin or API
rows.other: Defined in TypeScript config files, deployed with the app

rows.tess: Standalone Rust binary, any front-end stack
rows.other: Runs inside a Next.js (Node.js) application
REST, GraphQL and a local Node.js API

rows.tess: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB, RocksDB
rows.other: MongoDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite
TypeScript hooks and plugins in the app
MIT

competitors.chooseThem: - Your project is a Next.js app and you want the schema in your repository as TypeScript.
competitors.chooseTess:
- Admins must evolve models without developers or redeploys.
- Your front ends are not all JavaScript, or you want the CMS separate from the app.
competitors.migration: Payload collections and blocks map to Tess content types and components (blocks fields become `DYNAMIC_ZONE`). Translate the config into the `tess-transfer` YAML format, import it, and copy documents through the GraphQL APIs.

competitors.name: Sanity
competitors.kind: Hosted content platform with an open-source studio
competitors.summary: A hosted Content Lake with a customizable, open-source React editing studio and its own query language, GROQ.

rows.other: Hosted Content Lake; the studio is open source and self-deployable

rows.tess: Admin UI or API, applied immediately
rows.other: Schemas in JavaScript/TypeScript code
GROQ, plus a deployable GraphQL API

rows.tess: Admin UI with drafts and reviews
rows.other: Real-time collaborative editing in a highly customizable studio
Sanity's cloud

rows.tess: Community free for personal use; Enterprise license for commercial use
rows.other: Free tier, then paid plans by usage and seats

competitors.chooseThem: - You need real-time collaboration and a deeply customized editing studio.
competitors.chooseTess: - You want your content in your own database, with a standard GraphQL API and no query language to learn.
competitors.migration: Sanity document types and objects map to Tess content types and components; arrays of mixed types become `DYNAMIC_ZONE` fields. Import the models with `tess-transfer`, then copy documents from a Sanity export through the Tess GraphQL API.
